title: What It Actually Looks Like to Work Hard and Rest Well
caption:
A godly man works like the outcome depends on him. Then he stops, on purpose, like it never did.

Six days you shall labor, but the seventh is a Sabbath to the Lord your God (Exodus 20:9-10). That command showed up before hustle culture ever did. Sabbath was never a reward for a good week. It's an order for a man who forgets he isn't the one holding the world up.

In vain you rise early and stay up late eating the bread of anxious labor, while God gives sleep to the ones he loves (Psalm 127:2). If you can't stop, you've started believing the day runs on your hours.

And numbing out on a Sunday afternoon isn't rest either. Real rest costs you control: the phone in the drawer, the slow meal, the walk with no destination. The grind and the stillness are the same kind of trust, a man who believes God's the one actually keeping the wheels turning.

Save this for the next Sunday you can't sit still.
